learning_objective: 🎯 Discover why the world needs international organizations like the UN, how they function, and the pressing need to reform them for the 21st century!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Established in 1945 after WWII to prevent international conflict, facilitate cooperation, and tackle global issues like poverty and disease. It is the most important international organization today.
The UN functions through bodies like the General Assembly (where all nations have one vote) and the Security Council (the most powerful organ, dealing with global security).

main_concepts.concept_title: 🛑 The UN Security Council and Veto Power
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Security Council has 5 permanent members (US, Russia, UK, France, China) who possess 'Veto power'—the ability to single-handedly block any substantive resolution, often leading to gridlock.

Many countries, including India, argue that the UN’s structure is stuck in 1945. They demand reforms, especially the expansion of the Security Council to reflect modern global realities and give developing nations a voice.
Organizations like the World Bank, IMF, and WTO govern the global economy, while NGOs like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch hold governments accountable globally.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Be the UN Secretary-General
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are the head of the UN. If you could pass one universal law today to solve a global crisis (climate change, poverty, or war), what would it be? Write a short resolution explaining how you would enforce it.

exam_tips: 📌 Always list the 5 permanent members of the UN Security Council (P5) when discussing the Veto power.
📌 Be ready to argue why India deserves a permanent seat in the UN Security Council (population, economic growth, UN peacekeeping contributions).
📌 Understand the difference between the IMF (oversees global financial system) and the WTO (sets rules for global trade).
quick_recap: ⭐ The UN replaced the ineffective League of Nations in 1945.
⭐ The Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent with veto power, and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.
⭐ Despite its flaws and the dominance of major powers, the UN is considered indispensable for managing an increasingly interconnected world.
